turns:
This is a subscription-service unit economics problem. You must show your work.

Assumptions:
- Monthly subscription price $29.00, payment processing fee 3.4%
- Variable server/ops cost per customer per month: $4.20
- Average subscription lifetime: 14 months
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC): $68.00 per new customer from paid ads

Questions:
1. Monthly contribution margin ($) and contribution margin rate (%)? (1 decimal place)
2. LTV? (contribution margin × lifetime)
3. LTV/CAC ratio? (1 decimal place)
4. CAC payback period in months? (1 decimal place)
5. Marketing wants to raise CAC to $85.00 — judge whether that is acceptable against a 3x LTV/CAC threshold.

rubric.name: Calculation accuracy
rubric.desc: All 5 answers correct (1: $23.81 / 82.1%, 2: $333.40, 3: 4.9, 4: 2.9 months, 5: acceptable at 3.9x)

rubric.name: Clarity of work
rubric.desc: Calculation logic is presented so it is easy to follow

rubric.name: Judgment quality
rubric.desc: Question 5 mentions headroom versus the threshold and the risks

reference:
1. Contribution margin = 29.00 - 29.00*0.034 (=0.986) - 4.20 = $23.814 ≈ $23.81, contribution margin rate = 23.814/29.00 = 82.1%
2. LTV = 23.814 * 14 = $333.396 ≈ $333.40
3. LTV/CAC = 333.396/68.00 = 4.9
4. Payback period = 68.00/23.814 = 2.9 months
5. Even at $85.00, 333.396/85.00 = 3.9x ≥ 3, so it is acceptable (bonus for noting sensitivity of the lifetime assumption)
